sourcedFrom: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 (2001 — the copyright line on p.1 reads "02001 Colt Manufacturing Company, Inc." in the OCR, the © rendered as a zero)
cleanIntro: Colt's own dismounting procedure for the Woodsman, in the factory's words. This is one of the rare old books that publishes two levels: the strip needed for cleaning, and a complete dismounting beyond it — so this listing has a Deep Clean that is entirely the manufacturer's.

steps.title: Magazine out, then look into the chamber
steps.action: Press the magazine catch and remove the magazine, then look to see there is no cartridge left in the chamber.
steps.prose: Colt puts the chamber check inside the dismounting instruction itself, in parentheses, as though it were obvious. It is the step people skip.
steps.caution: (After removing magazine, look to see that there is no cartridge left in the chamber.)
steps.quote: TO DISMOUNT: Remove magazine by pressing the magazine catch.
steps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO DISMOUNT, unpaginated p.4 of 4

steps.title: Slide fully back, then hold the assembly lock plunger down
steps.action: With the pistol in the left hand, grasp the slide between the thumb and middle finger of the right hand and pull it to the rear as far as it will go. Then push down the assembly lock plunger on top of the slide with your index finger and, holding pressure on it, let the slide move forward to the closed position.
steps.prose: The plunger has to stay down the whole way forward. Release it early and the recoil spring guide re-locks, and the slide will not come off.
steps.quote: With pistol in left hand, grasp slide between thumb and middle finger of right hand and pull to rear as far as it will go.
steps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO DISMOUNT, unpaginated p.4 of 4

steps.title: Closed, pull the trigger, release the plunger
steps.action: With the slide fully closed, pull the trigger and then release pressure on the assembly lock plunger.
steps.prose: The trigger pull drops the hammer forward so the mainspring housing can come out. The chamber was checked two steps ago precisely so this is safe.
steps.quote: When fully closed, pull trigger and release pressure on assembly lock plunger.
steps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO DISMOUNT, unpaginated p.4 of 4

steps.title: Press the knurled mainspring housing up and in
steps.action: With the thumb of the right hand, press on the housing where it is knurled — pressure exerted upwards as well as inwards.
steps.prose: Up as well as in. Pressing straight in alone will not release it, and that is the whole reason Colt spells the direction out.
steps.quote: With thumb of right hand press on housing at point where same is knurled; pressure should be exerted upwards as well as in.
steps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO DISMOUNT, unpaginated p.4 of 4

steps.title: Housing out — and the magazine catch and sear spring with it
steps.action: The housing releases from the receiver and can be withdrawn. At the same time the magazine catch and sear spring, which are pinned together, are released and can be taken out of the pistol.
steps.prose: Two small parts leave with the housing. Expect them, or you will find them on the floor and not know what they are.
steps.quote: This will release housing from receiver and it may be withdrawn; at the same time magazine catch and Sear spring (which are pinned together) are released and can be taken from arm.
steps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO DISMOUNT, unpaginated p.4 of 4

steps.title: Slide rearward off the receiver
steps.action: Draw the slide rearward off the receiver.
steps.prose: Rearward on this pistol, not forward — the mainspring housing was the rear abutment holding it on, and with that gone the slide simply lifts off the back.
steps.quote: Slide can now be drawn rearward from receiver.
steps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO DISMOUNT, unpaginated p.4 of 4

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Receiver, slide, mainspring housing, magazine catch with sear spring, and magazine. Colt states plainly that this is all the dismounting cleaning requires.
steps.prose: That sentence is the manual telling you where routine care stops — the complete dismounting exists, but it is a different job with a different purpose.
steps.caution: If the recoil spring jars off the assembly lock during dismounting or assembly, press it forward again and hold it by pressing the assembly lock plunger down.
steps.quote: The foregoing is all the dismounting necessary to clean and properly care for the arm.
steps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO DISMOUNT, unpaginated p.4 of 4

deepSteps.title: Stocks off, side plate off
deepSteps.action: Remove the stocks, then remove the side plate screw and take off the side plate.
deepSteps.prose: The side plate is what covers the trigger, trigger bar and spring. Everything in this section is behind it.
deepSteps.quote: TO COMPLETE DISMOUNTING: Remove stocks. Remove side plate screw and then side plate.
deepSteps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO COMPLETE DISMOUNTING, unpaginated p.4 of 4

deepSteps.title: Lift out the safety lock — it is also the hammer pin
deepSteps.action: Lift the safety lock out of the receiver. On this pistol the safety lock doubles as the hammer pin, so the hammer is free once it is out.
deepSteps.prose: One part doing two jobs is why the hammer cannot come out first. Take the safety lock out and the hammer follows.
deepSteps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO COMPLETE DISMOUNTING, unpaginated p.4 of 4

deepSteps.title: Hammer and strut out
deepSteps.action: Remove the hammer and strut together. The strut may be separated from the hammer by driving out the strut pin.
deepSteps.prose: Leave the strut on the hammer unless it needs cleaning behind — the strut pin is small and does not want to be driven twice.
deepSteps.quote: Remove hammer and strut. Strut may be removed from hammer by driving out strut pin.
deepSteps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO COMPLETE DISMOUNTING, unpaginated p.4 of 4

deepSteps.title: Drive out the sear pin and drop the sear
deepSteps.action: Drive out the sear pin; the sear will drop out.
deepSteps.prose: Support the receiver so the pin has somewhere to go, and catch the sear rather than letting it fall.
deepSteps.quote: Next drive out sear pin permitting sear to drop out.
deepSteps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO COMPLETE DISMOUNTING, unpaginated p.4 of 4

deepSteps.title: Trigger, pivot spring and bar together
deepSteps.action: Take the trigger out by pressing against its right side; the same motion removes the trigger pivot, spring and bar.
deepSteps.prose: Three parts come out as one movement, so watch how they sit before they move — that is the picture you will need to reassemble against.
deepSteps.quote: The trigger can be taken out by pressing against right side and at same time this will remove trigger pivot spring and bar.
deepSteps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO COMPLETE DISMOUNTING, unpaginated p.4 of 4

deepSteps.title: Ejector out
deepSteps.action: Drive out the ejector pin, then remove the ejector from its slot in the top of the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: It is a small transverse pin holding a small part. A punch that fits is worth more than force here.
deepSteps.quote: Ejector can be removed by first driving out ejector pin.
deepSteps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO COMPLETE DISMOUNTING, unpaginated p.4 of 4

deepSteps.title: Firing pin out through the front of the slide
deepSteps.action: Take out the firing pin stop screw in the bottom of the slide, hold the slide vertically with the front end up, and the firing pin will drop out.
deepSteps.prose: Gravity does the work. If it does not drop, the stop screw is not fully out — do not poke at it.
deepSteps.quote: To remove firing pin and spring take out firing pin stop screw located in bottom of slide, hold slide in vertical position, front end up; firing pin will drop out.
deepSteps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO COMPLETE DISMOUNTING, unpaginated p.4 of 4

deepSteps.title: Block the extractor plunger, then lift the extractor
deepSteps.action: Press the extractor plunger back far enough to insert a pointed instrument through the small aperture; that blocks the plunger and lets the extractor be lifted out.
deepSteps.prose: The pin through the aperture is what holds the spring while your other hand works. Without it the plunger and spring leave together.
deepSteps.quote: this will block plunger and allow extractor to be lifted out.
deepSteps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO COMPLETE DISMOUNTING, unpaginated p.4 of 4

deepSteps.title: Leave the barrel alone
deepSteps.action: Do not remove the barrel. It is screwed into a long seat in the receiver and Colt's own instruction is to leave it there.
deepSteps.prose: The threaded seat is what gives this pistol its rigidity and its accuracy. Nothing about cleaning requires disturbing it.
deepSteps.quote: It is advisable not to remove barrel.
deepSteps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO COMPLETE DISMOUNTING, unpaginated p.4 of 4

deepSteps.title: Magazine apart, if it needs it
deepSteps.action: Press the follower down until the follower pin can be withdrawn through the aperture on the right side of the magazine. The follower rises to the top and comes out by turning its front top to the rear so the lugs pass under the cartridge spring ears; then remove the spring.
deepSteps.prose: The thumb piece on the right side is the follower pin, which is why it can be pushed out from outside the tube.
deepSteps.quote: The magazine may be dismounted readily by pressing down follower until follower pin can be withdrawn through aperture on right side of magazine.
deepSteps.cite: Colt "Woodsman" Automatic Pistol, Caliber .22 Long Rifle — Form M-90 — TO COMPLETE DISMOUNTING, unpaginated p.4 of 4

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: Always clean and oil the inside of the barrel and the chamber as soon after firing as possible
The slide comes off the back, so the Woodsman can be cleaned from the breech end — Colt lists that as one of the design's advantages
A .22 rimfire fouls with wax and lead as much as with powder; work at the chamber mouth as well as the bore

cleaning.name: SLIDE AND RECEIVER
tasks: Keep the slide grooves clean and well oiled
Clean the breech face, the extractor cut and the ejector slot while the slide is off
Wipe the recoil spring and guide and the assembly lock area, and check the assembly lock plunger moves freely

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Occasionally put a few drops of light oil in the magazine
Never use heavy oil — Colt says so in the same sentence
Clean carbon and wax off the follower and the cartridge spring ears

reassembly: Place the slide on the receiver and push it forward to the closed position.
Insert the magazine catch and sear spring, making sure the lug on the magazine catch fits into its slot in the handle, with the sear spring resting on the sear and under the hammer strut.
The hammer must be in the forward position with the hammer strut resting on the sear spring — pull the trigger to be sure the hammer is fully forward.
Place the top of the mainspring housing under the end of the receiver and resting on the sear spring, then press on its lower end so it snaps into place.
If the recoil spring jars off the assembly lock at any point, press it forward again and hold it by pressing down the assembly lock plunger.
To load afterwards, draw the slide back, lock it open with the safety, insert the magazine and let the slide return forward.
fncheck: Remember that drawing the slide to the rear cocks the pistol and leaves it ready to fire. With the magazine out and the chamber checked, work the slide and confirm the safety lock rises into its recess in the slide and locks both slide and hammer, and that it presses down freely again.
